capitals.name: Ceuta (Sabta)
capitals.note: The pages give no infobox and name no other seat; Ceuta is the taifa's name and city.

correction.text: Ceuta and Tangier, held by the Barghawata after they 'took power from the Hammudids' shortly before 1061

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Taifa of Ceuta page has the Barghawata, 'led by the illiterate Saqqut', seize power shortly before 1061 (453 AH) and the Ceuta page has Suqut al-Bargawati 'styling as a caliph after 1061' (the link with Málaga was severed in 1056); Cliopatria's row starts in 1066. The pages give no boundary except that Ceuta and Tangier were part of the Hammudid taifa of Málaga from 1026, so Cliopatria's 1066 shape is carried back; unverified: page budget.

1,476 km2 (6 cells, from the Tetouan coast to Tangier), 1066-1071; no infobox area (page silent). It matches the only extent the pages give, 'Ceuta and Tangier'. The pages say nothing of Seville, which Cliopatria lists as a neighbour.

1,351 km2 (5 cells): the eastern coastal cell near 35.7 N 5.3 W is dropped from 1072 and no page opened says why. It runs to 1084, the year the Ceuta page gives for the Almoravid rule ('Starting in 1084, the Almoravid Berbers ruled the region until 1147'); the Taifa of Ceuta page instead has the Almoravid conquest in 1078-79, so the shape may run five years too long. Cliopatria's Almoravid shape contains the Ceuta cells from 1085, which sides with 1084.

ledger.note: 1061: the Barghawata make Ceuta independent of the Hammudids. 'Shortly before 1061 (453 AH), the Barghawata, led by the illiterate Saqqut, took power from the Hammudids'; the Ceuta page: 'In 1056, the link with Malaga was severed as it was conquered by the Banu Ziri, while Suqut al-Bargawati remained in power in Ceuta, styling as a caliph after 1061'. The Barghawata had governed Ceuta on behalf of the Hammudids from 1036. The page names Ceuta and Tangier as the land (both in the Hammudid taifa of Málaga from 1026).

1084: the Almoravids take Ceuta. 'Starting in 1084, the Almoravid Berbers ruled the region until 1147, when the Almohads conquered the land' (Ceuta page). The Taifa of Ceuta page dates the conquest 'by the rising power of the Almoravids in 1078-79'; Cliopatria and the Ceuta page agree on 1084, which this ledger follows.
1084: the taifa of Ceuta ends under the Almoravids (1078-79 on the Taifa of Ceuta page).

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of Ceuta
wars.outcome: The taifa 'conquered by the rising power of the Almoravids in 1078-79' (Taifa of Ceuta page) or ruled by them 'starting in 1084' (Ceuta page); the Almoravids hold the region until the Almohads take it in 1147.
wars.note: The two pages disagree on the year and neither describes the campaign; the span is the two dates.

certainty.note: A small Berber principality round Ceuta and Tangier; the pages give no frontier.

notes: Cliopatria's row (1066-1084, two shapes of 6 and 5 cells) is a small Berber principality round Ceuta and Tangier. The pages give no area, boundary or neighbour. Page conflict: the Almoravid conquest is '1078-79' on the Taifa of Ceuta page and 'starting in 1084' on the Ceuta page; Cliopatria and this dossier take 1084. Founding: 'shortly before 1061' (taifa page) against the severance from Málaga in 1056 (Ceuta page); this dossier starts in 1061 and carries Cliopatria's 1066 shape back, unverified (page budget). The Hammudid Taifa of Málaga, from which Ceuta separated, has no Cliopatria row and no dossier in this group (suggested slug taifa-of-malaga; the Zirids who took Málaga in 1056 are the Zirid taifa of Granada, taifa-of-granada (the Taifa page lists 'Málaga: 1026–1057/1058 (to Granada)'), not zirid-dynasty). Not settled (page silent): Saqqut's reign years and the rulers' list; the neighbour taifa-of-seville in Cliopatria; why the 1072 shape drops a cell. Counterparts: almoravid-dynasty (af-02). Page budget (1-2): Taifa of Ceuta, Ceuta.
